chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman al-Naysaburi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Zakariyya, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, all together, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Saeed Aqeysa al-Taymi, who said:

I passed by al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and they were in the Euphrates, soaking their lower garments. So I said to them, 'O sons of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)! Have you spoiled your lower garments?' They said to me, 'O Abu Saeed! The spoiling of our lower garments is more beloved to us than the spoiling of the Religion. Indeed, for the water there are its rightful ones and dwellers, like the dwellers of the earth.'

Then they said, 'Where do you intend to go?' I said, 'To this water.' They said, 'And what is this water?' I said, 'I want its remedy; I drink from this bitter water for an ailment in me, hoping that the body will lighten and the belly will be eased.' They said, 'We do not reckon that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made healing in something which He has cursed.' I said, 'And why is that?' They said, 'Because when Allah, Blessed and High, was angered by the people of Noah (peace be upon him), He opened the sky with a downpour of water, and revealed to the earth. But certain springs from it disobeyed Him, so He cursed them and made them salty and bitter.'

And in the narration of Hamdan ibn Suleyman, they (peace be upon them) said, 'O Abu Saeed! You have come to a water which denies our Wilayah three times each day. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, presented our Wilayah to the waters; so whatever accepted our Wilayah became fresh and sweet, and whatever denied our Wilayah, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made it bitter or salty and burning.'
ai.seo_question: Why is some water bitter or salty according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'Wilayah al-Ma' (the authority of the Imams over water), where the Euphrates' salinity is interpreted as a cosmic sign of denial of their divine station, contrasting with sweet water that accepts their Wilayah. By linking the bitter springs to Noah's flood, the Imams establish a theological precedent where physical properties of creation reflect spiritual realities, reinforcing the Shia belief in the Imams' influence over the natural world.
